stale/ask: A model knows what it read in training. Ask about something that has changed since, like the library's Sunday hours, and it answers from that old text.
stale/context: In-context learning showed a fix: put the facts in the prompt. The model reads them there, and no weight changes.
stale/which: But the library's pages may hold thousands of passages, far too many for one prompt. Retrieval picks the few that match the question.
score/embed: An embedding model turns any text into a vector, so that texts about the same thing point the same way. Embed the question, and every passage once, ahead of time.
score/size: Each vector is scaled to size one: its squared entries add up to one. Then a dot product sees only direction: one when two vectors point the same way, zero at a right angle. It is called cosine similarity.
score/score: The question is zero point six, zero point eight. Passage zero, zero point eight, zero point six, scores zero point four eight plus zero point four eight: zero point nine six.
score/rest: Passage one, one and zero, scores zero point six. Passage two, at a right angle, scores zero.
score/top: Keep the top k. With k of two, that is passages zero and one.
prompt/build: Put the top passages into the prompt, before the question.
prompt/answer: The model reads the current hours in its context and answers from them: noon. Its weights never changed.
prompt/update: When the hours change again, embed the new page and swap it into the collection. No model is retrained.
prompt/cost: The passages do take room in the context: two of two hundred tokens before a question of ten make four hundred ten tokens.
